To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GME estimators are consistent and asymptoticaly normal, that the asymptotic variance of a GME estimator is equal to the inverse of the expected Fisher information matrix, and that the asymptotic normality of the GME estimators can be used for hypothesis testing.
GME estimators are consistent, asymptotically normal, and asymptotically unbiased; they have a computationally efficient algorithm; and the asymptotic variances of GME estimations can be computed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of estimators for the general linear model, which is consistent, asymptotically normal, and computationally efficient.
the theoretical properties of the data-constrained GME estimator, the computational efficiency of this estimator, and the statistical properties of the resulting estimates.
developing a general methodology for estimating the parameters of a GLM, and we provide a comprehensive treatment of the asymptotic properties of the GME method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, GME estimation is not a good idea, but there may be special cases in which it is.
, for large sample size, the data-constrained GME estimator of a GLM parameter has the same asymptotic distribution as the MLE.
the GME method is an efficient and unbiased estimator, and that the method is a useful alternative to the maximum likelihood method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the data constrained maximum entropy estimator of a general linear model is asymptotically efficient, and is asymptotically equivalent to a Bayesian estimator that uses a uniform prior on the parameter space.
the GME estimator is an efficient estimator of the GLM parameters when the prior distribution of the model parameters is uniform.

we have provided an analytical foundation for GME estimators, have developed computationally efficient procedures for calculating GME estimators and for performing statistical inference, and have identified a new variant of the GEM estimator that is unbiased.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GME is a useful and flexible alternative for parameter estimation in the GLM.
GME estimators can be applied in situations where Bayesian methods are not feasible.
the GME estimator is a useful and efficient alternative to Bayesian estimation, and that the asymptotic properties we derive can be used to conduct statistical inference.
